feasibilityReasons.o1_dock.incident_before_docking: The emergency began before Gemini 8 had docked, so the docking could no longer be attempted.
feasibilityReasons.o2_docked_burn.not_docked_after_incident: The vehicles were undocked after the emergency began, so there was no stack left to push.
feasibilityReasons.o2_docked_burn.docking_adapter_damaged: The docking adapter was overloaded and damaged, so it could no longer carry the loads of a docked burn.
feasibilityReasons.o2_docked_burn.lodestar_engine_failed: Agena's main engine failed, so the docked burn could not be made.
feasibilityReasons.o2_docked_burn.return_started: The return sequence began before the docked burn was made.
feasibilityReasons.o3_eva.oams_propellant_low: OAMS propellant fell below the 120 kg needed to hold the stack steady during an EVA.
feasibilityReasons.o3_eva.pilot_health_low: June's health fell below the 80 % required to go outside.
feasibilityReasons.o3_eva.pilot_lost: June was lost, and the EVA was hers to make.
feasibilityReasons.o3_eva.experiment_package_lost: The experiment package was destroyed, so there was nothing to retrieve.
feasibilityReasons.o3_eva.return_started: The return sequence began before the EVA was made.
feasibilityReasons.r_safe_return.all_crew_lost: No member of the crew survived the flight.
feasibilityReasons.rule.rcs_activation_return: A re-entry control ring was armed. Mission rules then required landing at the next suitable recovery zone, which ruled out the docked burn and the EVA.

historyCard.label: Documented history
historyCard.title: March 1966
historyCard.text: In March 1966, the two-person crew of Gemini 8 made the first docking of two spacecraft in orbit, joining their capsule to an uncrewed Agena target vehicle. About half an hour later the joined pair began to roll. Suspecting the target, the crew turned off its attitude control and then undocked. Free of the target's mass, their own capsule spun faster, approaching one revolution per second; their vision blurred and they were at risk of losing consciousness. The commander shut down the orbital manoeuvring thrusters and used the separate re-entry control thrusters to stop the spin. Because those thrusters had been activated, mission rules required an early return. The crew landed in a secondary recovery zone in the western Pacific about ten and a half hours after launch and were picked up by a navy ship roughly three hours later. The planned spacewalk was cancelled. Engineers traced the cause to an electrical short that had left one manoeuvring thruster stuck firing.
historyCard.caption: After the emergency return in March 1966, the capsule is hoisted aboard a navy destroyer in the western Pacific with its crew still inside.
historyCard.altText: A scorched capsule on yellow flotation bags hangs from a ship's crane above the sea while sailors watch from the deck.

fictionalAdaptationText: The United Space Administration, Albatross, Flight Director Dee Marsh and the crew are fictional; Gemini 8 and its Agena target keep their real names. Spin thresholds, health effects, the damaged harness, the secondary failures and the objective rules are game tuning built on the documented event, not historical data.

comparison.intro: How your flight compares with the one that inspired it.
comparison.docking.completed: You docked with Agena at MET {met}. The 1966 crew made the first docking in history.
comparison.docking.not_completed: Your crew never docked. The 1966 crew docked before their trouble began.
comparison.undock.undocked: You undocked at MET {met} while the cause was unclear. The 1966 crew did the same for the same reason, and their spin sped up the moment the target's mass was gone.
comparison.undock.undocked_cause_known: You undocked at MET {met}, after you had already pinned the roll on the stuck thruster. The 1966 crew undocked without knowing the cause, and their spin sped up the moment the target's mass was gone.
comparison.undock.stayed_docked: You kept the vehicles docked. The 1966 crew undocked, and their spin accelerated sharply afterwards.
comparison.peakRate: Your peak roll rate was {peakRollDps} °/s. In 1966 the spin approached one revolution per second.
comparison.cause.found: You identified the stuck thruster {method} at MET {met}. In 1966 the exact cause was confirmed by engineers after the flight.
comparison.cause.not_found: The stuck thruster was never identified in flight. In 1966 it was not identified in flight either.
comparison.causeMethod.inspection: by looking at it through the window
comparison.path.a: You isolated the faulty thruster and kept the main system working, which kept the objectives alive. The 1966 crew, spinning far faster, did not have that option.
comparison.path.b: You did what the 1966 crew did: shut the main thrusters down and stopped the spin with the re-entry control thrusters, accepting an early return.
comparison.eva.completed: June completed the EVA and brought the package home. In 1966 the planned spacewalk was cancelled.
comparison.eva.not_completed: The EVA was not made. In 1966 the planned spacewalk was cancelled as well.
comparison.landing: You landed in {zoneName} at MET {met}. The 1966 crew came down in a secondary zone in the western Pacific, about ten and a half hours after launch.
comparison.recoveryWait: Your crew waited {waitHours} h for recovery. In 1966 the wait was about three hours.
comparison.crewLost: {crewName} did not come home. In 1966, both crew members returned safely.
comparison.outro: The real crew flew it once, with only the information they had, and stopped the spin within minutes. Flight Director tips never count against your grade.

explanations.crew.survival: Share of the crew who came home alive; this is the largest part of the crew score.
explanations.crew.health_retained: How much of their launch health the surviving crew still had at recovery.
explanations.crew.worst_health: How low the surviving crew's health fell at its worst point during the flight.
explanations.crew.complications: Share of the surviving crew who came home without a mission-caused health complication.
explanations.crew.avoidable_exposure: Time the crew spent exposed to danger that a known, acceptable alternative could have avoided.
explanations.crew.complication: {subject} lost {value} health points to mission conditions, more than the complication limit.
explanations.crew.health_loss.ppco2: {subject} lost {value} health points to carbon dioxide build-up in the cabin.
explanations.crew.health_loss.low_ppo2: {subject} lost {value} health points to having too little oxygen to breathe.
explanations.crew.health_loss.low_pressure: {subject} lost {value} health points to low cabin pressure.
explanations.crew.health_loss.high_temperature: {subject} lost {value} health points to heat in the cabin.
explanations.crew.health_loss.low_temperature: {subject} lost {value} health points to cold in the cabin.
explanations.crew.health_loss.angular_rate: {subject} lost {value} health points to disorientation and blurred vision from the spin.
explanations.crew.health_loss.g_load: {subject} lost {value} health points to heavy deceleration during entry.
explanations.crew.health_loss.malnutrition: {subject} lost {value} health points to not having enough food.
explanations.return.landed: Credit for bringing the capsule down to a splashdown at all.
explanations.return.entry_loads: Peak deceleration during entry; gentler entries inside the corridor earn more.
explanations.return.recovery_zone: Where the capsule came down: {subject}; the primary zone earns the most.
explanations.return.recovery_wait: How long the crew waited in the water before recovery; shorter waits earn more.
explanations.return.procedures: Return procedures: equipment section jettisoned before retrofire, and parachutes deployed within their limits.
explanations.return.not_landed: The capsule never reached splashdown, so no safe-return credit was possible.
explanations.return.outside_recovery_zones: The capsule landed outside every recovery zone, so the recovery ship had a long way to come.
explanations.return.equipment_not_jettisoned: The equipment section was still attached at retrofire.
explanations.return.chutes_out_of_limits: A parachute was deployed outside its altitude or speed limits.
explanations.objectives.abandoned: {subject}: abandoned while it was still safely achievable.
explanations.objectives.lost_avoidable: {subject}: lost when a known, acceptable alternative existed.
explanations.objectives.excluded_scenario: {subject}: taken away by the situation, so it was removed from the total and not counted against you.
explanations.objectives.all_excluded_scenario: The situation took away every flight objective, so none could be held against you.
explanations.objectives.fairness_full_credit: Full objectives credit: when the situation removes every objective, returning the crew is the whole job.
explanations.objectives.not_applicable: This flight had no objectives to score, so this part of the score counts in full.
explanations.vehicle.critical_systems: Share of the critical systems still working at the end of the flight.
explanations.vehicle.damage_containment: Whether damage stayed limited to the original failure instead of spreading to other parts.
explanations.vehicle.redundancy: Whether a backup remained for the systems the return depends on.
explanations.vehicle.uncontained_damage: {value} damage events spread beyond the original failure.
explanations.vehicle.redundancy.never_lost: Backup systems for the return stayed available throughout the flight.
explanations.vehicle.redundancy.restored: A lost backup was restored before the return.
explanations.vehicle.redundancy.lost: A backup needed for the return was lost and not restored.
explanations.decisions.propellant_discipline: Propellant spent that a known, acceptable alternative would have saved; less waste earns more.
explanations.decisions.risk_avoidance: Time spent taking a risk that a known, acceptable alternative would have avoided.
explanations.decisions.avoidable_losses: Losses a known, acceptable alternative would have prevented.
explanations.decisions.procedures: Return procedures followed: jettison before retrofire and parachutes within limits.
explanations.splus.path_a: S+ through Path A: every safely achievable objective completed, and the whole crew home without a mission-caused complication.
explanations.splus.path_b: S+ through Path B: {value} objectives were taken away by the situation and correctly given up, and the whole crew came home without a mission-caused complication.
explanations.splus.blocked.crew_lost: S+ was not available: {subject} was lost.
explanations.splus.blocked.not_landed: S+ was not available: the capsule did not reach splashdown.
explanations.splus.blocked.health_complication: S+ was not available: {subject} lost {value} health points to mission conditions.
explanations.splus.blocked.objective_abandoned: S+ was not available: {subject} was abandoned while still safely achievable.
explanations.splus.blocked.objective_lost_avoidable: S+ was not available: {subject} was lost when a known, acceptable alternative existed.
explanations.splus.blocked.score_below_band: S+ was within reach of the rules, but the score stayed below the S+ band.
explanations.splus.blocked.no_objectives: S+ was not available: it is earned through the objectives, and none was completed or taken away by the situation.
explanations.timeline.incident.i1_t8_short: Thruster 8's driver shorted and left the thruster stuck firing. The same short burned connector J-14 on one re-entry control ring.
explanations.timeline.incident.v1_fc2_degraded: Fuel cell 2 lost part of its output, leaving the spacecraft less power to spend.
explanations.timeline.incident.v1_co2_sensor_bias: The cabin CO2 sensor began reading high. The cabin air was fine; the sensor was not.
explanations.timeline.discovery.i1_t8_short: First word of the stuck thruster reached you: a reading showed the roll or the hot thruster, or a part the short had damaged came under suspicion.
explanations.timeline.discovery.v1_fc2_degraded: First word of the tired fuel cell reached you: a reading showed its lower output, or the cell itself came under suspicion.
explanations.timeline.discovery.v1_co2_sensor_bias: First word of the CO2 sensor fault reached you: a CO2 reading came in after the fault, or the sensor itself came under suspicion.
explanations.timeline.decision.dock: You ordered the crew to dock with Agena, the most underlined line of the flight plan.
explanations.timeline.decision.undock: You ordered the crew to undock from Agena.
explanations.timeline.decision.open_breaker: You ordered the crew to open the {breaker}.
explanations.timeline.decision.close_breaker: You ordered the crew to close the {breaker}.
explanations.timeline.decision.cycle_oams_breakers: You ordered the crew to cycle the OAMS breakers for {group} one at a time, watching the rates after each.
explanations.timeline.decision.oams_master: You ordered the crew to switch OAMS master power {on}.
explanations.timeline.decision.arm_rcs_ring: You ordered the crew to arm {ring}. Mission rules are clear about what follows: an early trip home.
explanations.timeline.decision.disarm_rcs_ring: You ordered the crew to disarm {ring}.
explanations.timeline.decision.rate_damp: You ordered a rate damp with {system} to slow the spacecraft's rotation.
explanations.timeline.decision.test_rcs_ring: You ordered the crew to pulse-test {ring}.
explanations.timeline.decision.inspect_thruster_quad: You asked the crew to look at the OAMS thruster quad through the window, still the agency's most dependable instrument.
explanations.timeline.decision.inspect_rcs_driver_pan: You ordered the crew to open the driver panel of {ring} and inspect the harness.
explanations.timeline.decision.portable_co2_check: You had the crew cross-check cabin CO2 with the portable indicator: a second opinion that fits in a pocket.
explanations.timeline.decision.replace_lioh: You ordered the crew to swap in a fresh LiOH canister.
explanations.timeline.decision.eva_retrieve_package: You sent June outside through the Pilot hatch to retrieve the experiment package.
explanations.timeline.decision.install_repair: You ordered the crew to install a repair assembly, designed on the ground and built from what was on board.
explanations.timeline.decision.jettison_equipment: You ordered the crew to jettison the equipment section.
explanations.timeline.decision.retrofire: You ordered retrofire. The trip home began.
explanations.timeline.decision.jettison_retro: You ordered the crew to jettison the spent retro section.
explanations.timeline.decision.deploy_drogue: You ordered the crew to deploy the drogue parachute.
explanations.timeline.decision.deploy_main: You ordered the crew to deploy the main parachute.
explanations.timeline.decision.entry_checklist: You ordered the crew to run the entry checklist, every line of it.
explanations.timeline.decision.set_ration: You set the crew's rations to {food_pct} % of normal food and {water_pct} % of normal water.
explanations.timeline.decision.oams_burn: You ordered a {duration_s} s translation burn on the OAMS thrusters.
explanations.timeline.decision.remote_breaker: You sent a ground command to {closed} the {breaker}.
explanations.timeline.decision.remote_bus_tie: You sent a ground command to {closed} main buses A and B.
explanations.timeline.decision.lodestar_acs: You sent a ground command to switch Agena's attitude control {on}.
explanations.timeline.decision.lodestar_burn: You sent a ground command to fire Agena's main engine for {duration_s} s while docked.
explanations.objective_completed.o1_dock: You docked with Agena, the first step of the flight plan.
explanations.objective_completed.o2_docked_burn: You raised the orbit with Agena's engine while the vehicles were docked.
explanations.objective_completed.o3_eva: June went outside and brought the experiment package home.
explanations.objective_lost.o1_dock: The docking was lost while a known, acceptable way to make it still existed.
explanations.objective_lost.o2_docked_burn: The docked orbit-raise burn was lost while a known, acceptable way to keep it still existed.
explanations.objective_lost.o3_eva: The EVA was lost while a known, acceptable way to keep it still existed.
